reason: Four defects in the proposed falsifier. (1) 'Verify c/x is affine' and '(a)=(b)' are algebraic identities, not experiments. c/x = a^2+sa+N exactly, and a->a^2+sa is F_2-linear (kernel {0,s}). Arms (a) and (b) differ only by an invertible F_2-linear change of the descent coordinates. The Boolean ideal <v^2+v> is invariant under affine F_2 maps, so the Macaulay rank profile at every degree D is exactly equal. msolve's grevlex F4 max-degree is NOT invariant under linear changes, so 'exactly equal' will fail on msolve noise alone and would be read as a spurious refutation. Arm (a) is a pipeline unit test, not a discriminator. (2) The only informative comparison is (b) vs (c), and the prediction '(c) within +-1' does not follow from 'Mobius relabelling'. x->1/x is not F_2-linear, so the 1/x base is a different set. In Y=1/x the descended S_3 has the shape a6*YR^2*c^2+YR*c=(Y1+Y2+YR)^2 with c=Y1*Y2, which is F_2-linear(c)=linear. It is structurally parallel to the x-form u^2+XR*u=XR^2*v^2+a6 but not isomorphic. So (b)-(c)=0 or +-1 is a hypothesis, not a theorem, and it is a genuine presentation-dependence test; the brief already records d_F as presentation-dependent. (3) Confound: arm (b) is an AFFINE subspace in 1/x (offset kappa with Tr=1) and arm (c) is LINEAR in x. The linear structure carries the Frobenius witness mu=xR^-2 (d_ff<=2). Any difference could come from the offset alone, not the inversion. The torus family is exactly the ell-dim affine subspaces of the trace-1 hyperplane {y:Tr(y)=1} (theta -> theta+t just translates V). A random affine subspace in 1/x is in that hyperplane with prob ~2^-ell, so 'generic 1/x-affine' is not the torus family. The design needs affine-x and generic-affine-1/x controls. (4) Grid and parameters: m is unspecified. At m=2 the brief says the subspace shape is closed, and lever 1 lives at m>=3. At m=3 the regime needs m*ell <= n, so ell=3..6 at n=13 is underdetermined for ell>=5 and solving degree is meaningless there. n=17 has ord_17(2)=8, so it is unlike n=131 (ord=n-1); use n with ord_n(2)=n-1 (11,13,19,29). 'Strictly below at all l' on one draw is not a statistic: the variance comes from the subspace/curve draw, not the 50 targets. msolve wall time is irrelevant but its step degree is a noisy proxy. Fixable within budget with the redesign below. Scaling to n=131: a constant offset in d_F is engineering at best and cannot change an exponent, so the toy can only support a statement about the SLOPE of D vs ell at fixed m (extrapolated to ell~43 at m=3). Only slope-difference or growth in the 1/x arm would be a lever-1 finding.
fix: REDESIGN. Drop 'verify affine' and arm (a)=(b) as experiments; keep them as an exhaustive identity assertion (n=13: all a in F_q, check c/x == a^2+s*a+N and that the map is F_2-linear; seconds in python) and as a pipeline sanity check on the Macaulay rank profile (must match exactly; any mismatch is a bug). ARMS, all with the same curve y^2+xy=x^3+a6 (a2=0 or 1 per harness), same m, same ell, same target set: C0 = random ell-dim LINEAR F_2-subspace in x (baseline; must reproduce the brief's fit D=ceil(ell/2)+4 at m=3 as a positive control). C1 = random AFFINE subspace in x (random offset). T1 = TORUS arm: x=1/y, y in W+w with W=L(V) for random V (ell-dim, 1 not in V), w with Tr(w)=1 (equivalently a random affine ell-subspace of {Tr=1}, then map y->1/y). G1 = GENERIC affine subspace in 1/x (random W, random w, no trace constraint). NULL = two independent draws of C0 (gives the draw-to-draw noise floor for any 'difference'). Also random_matched systems from ffd_semaev_core as a degree-profile null. Contrasts: C0 vs C1 isolates the offset; C1 vs G1 isolates inversion at fixed affine-ness; G1 vs T1 isolates the trace-1 constraint. GRID: n in {13,19} (both ord_n(2)=n-1), m=3 (S_4 via intermediate variable X: S3(x1,x2,X)=0, S3(X,x3,xR)=0, F_2 coordinates of X free; Boolean with v^2+v) with (n,ell) = (13,3),(13,4),(19,4),(19,5),(19,6); also m=2 for ell=3..6 at n=19 as a cheap extra since ffd_semaev_core handles it; skip underdetermined cells (m*ell>n only when ell>n/m). SAMPLING: 20 independent (curve a6, basis, offset) draws per arm per cell x 2 targets (one decomposable by construction R=sum of base points, one random), stratify SAT/UNSAT in the reporting. METRICS (structural, not time): (i) Macaulay rank profile / first fall degree d_ff and, where feasible, last fall degree d_F via the existing harness (rank vs D is exactly invariant under linear coordinate change and makes arm comparisons exact); (ii) msolve -v 2 -g 2 F4 step-table max deg as a secondary witness with a 20 s cap per run, NOT the primary because grevlex is not linearly invariant; (iii) exact yield: number of ordered m-decompositions of random targets by enumeration (2^(m*ell) <= 2^18 combos) in PARI, ratio vs C0. Record per-cell medians/IQR and paired bootstrap CI of the T1-C0 and G1-C1 degree differences. DECISION RULE (pre-registered): 'relabelling' confirmed if every cell's median difference is within the NULL arm's spread AND the fitted slope of D vs ell (m=3, 5 cells) differs from C0's by < 0.25 AND yield ratio in [0.8,1.25]. 'Presentation lever' flagged only if T1 or G1 is below C0/C1 by >= 1 degree in >= 3 of 5 cells beyond the null spread, in the same direction, AND the slope is lower; even then classify as engineering (constant offset) unless the slope shrinks, and say the n=131 claim needs ell up to ~43, i.e. unmeasured. Budget: ~5 cells x 5 arms x 20 draws x 2 targets = 1000 runs; rank-profile arm at <0.3 s each plus msolve capped, fits ~15-20 CPU-min; if msolve exceeds it, cut msolve to 8 draws/arm and keep rank profile at 20. Tools: python3 + ffd_semaev_core (S_3, m=2) + own S_3-chain builder for m=3, gp for yield, msolve for secondary. No Sage.
